translated: Yay!
That's right.
I love looking at the ocean, so I booked a nice room where I could see the water and just spent the whole trip enjoying the view.
And you had dinner on the ship too?
Yeah, it was a buffet, but since the ship was rocking, everyone was being so careful while carrying their food.
That makes sense.
It was pretty funny. There were quite a few solo travelers, but because of the timing, there were a lot of families too.
I kept thinking how much fun it would be to have an experience like this as a kid.
I just watched the families while I ate my meal.
That sounds amazing.
So, what did you do once you arrived in Hokkaido?
I went to another place to stay, over in Otaru.
The ocean was beautiful there too. Apparently, Otaru is considered one of the three best scenic spots in Hokkaido.
Oh, really?
Yeah, so I stayed at a slightly expensive inn with a great view of the ocean.
I just spent my time soaking in the hot springs and eating delicious food.
Since I was alone, I could do whatever I wanted.
Treating yourself is important.
It really is. It's been a while since I spent that much money on a trip, but...
Well, that's exactly what you should spend it on.
Exactly.
Plus, there's no cell service on the ship. They had Wi-Fi, but...
Oh, right.
On the ship I took, you could only use it twice for 30 minutes each.
So in a way, it was like a digital detox. I brought books to read,
and I have a notebook where I write down things about acting and work.
I used that to reflect on things. It really felt like a solo journey.
That sounds so fulfilling.
It seems like you could really focus that way.
I really could.
